messages:
sara: Nightly eval flagged a regression for model-14 v2 (weights-only) on the legal_qa promptset — lots of truncation and wrong citation snippets. dropping details here for triage.

nightly-evals-bot: Nightly summary: model-14 v2 vs v1 -> pass_rate 82% -> 65% , avg_answer_len 320 -> 210, citation_accuracy 0.74 -> 0.52. Diff report: https://internal/reports/nightly/2398765432 (full logs + examples) :warning:

matt: Can you paste one representative bad generation inline?

sara: Here’s a repro (sanitized):
```
Prompt: "Summarize the key precedents for contract voidability and cite statutes."
Model v1 (expected): "... The court relied on Smith v. Jones (2015) and cited Stat. 12.4(a)..."
Model v2 (bad): "... The court relied on Smith v. Jones (2015) and cited Stat."  <-- truncation, missing citation text
```

jordan: Hmm from older notes v2 changed tokenizer normalization (punctuation collapsing). Could be token_count differences causing early stopping. saw similar with vX earlier.

alex: Also weird: our int8 quantized variant didn't show the same failure locally; only the hosted nightly run. Could be runtime-level KV cache alignment or padding behavior.

sara: Quick ngram check: truncation correlates with long prefix tokens > 280. Hypothesis: new kernel path drops trailing tokens when padding > 0. Sharing minimal repro command: 
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/generate -d '{"model":"model-14:v2","prompt":"<long prompt>...","max_tokens":200}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $RWD'
```

matt: Assigning: @jordan -> look into tokenizer diffs (v1 vs v2), @alex -> check runtime/kv cache + padding codepath, @sara -> run a small eval forcing the old tokenizer on v2 and post results.

sara: :thumbsup: running forced-old-tokenizer eval now, will post in ~30m.

nightly-evals-bot: Note: canary rollback trigger exists (v2 -> v1) for customer canaries but full nightly still used v2. ops notified.

alex: Quick grep shows model manifest v2 has `tokenizer_preproc: {norm: true}` while v1 used `norm: false`. If that's the root cause, we can temporarily flip the field in the manifest for nightly.

jordan: Good catch. We should also add a small tokenizer-compat check to nightly: compare token counts on anchor prompts and fail on >5% delta.

sara: Uploaded failing example + minimal repro to s3: s3://redwood-nightly/repro/model14/v2/2398765432.json. Also added to promptset repro folder.

matt: Thanks. Quick sync in 20 to decide rollback vs manifest tweak. If anyone finds a trivial rollback path, prefer canary rollback first.

alex: I'll try a manifest toggle on a staging canary and report back in 15.

sara: I'll paste the eval diffs here once the forced-tokenizer run finishes.
